title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.

providers.name: Databricks (AWS baseline)
providers.scope_notes: AWS IP-access-list docs require Enterprise tier. Azure/GCP capabilities and licensing must be checked separately.

controls.name: Personal Access Tokens (workspace toggle)
controls.what: Turns off PAT authentication for a workspace; existing tokens are not deleted.
controls.setting: Workspace Settings > Advanced > Personal Access Tokens
controls.quote: enabled by default for all Databricks workspaces.

controls.name: Personal access token permissions (CAN USE)
controls.what: Restricts which users, groups and service principals can create and use PATs.
controls.setting: Workspace Settings > Advanced > Personal Access Tokens > Permissions; Permissions API
controls.quote: User cannot create or use personal access tokens to authenticate to the Databricks workspace.

controls.name: maxTokenLifetimeDays
controls.what: Caps lifetime of new PATs (default 730 days); does not affect existing tokens.

controls.name: Automatic revocation of unused PATs
controls.what: PATs not used for 90 days are revoked automatically.
controls.quote: Databricks automatically revokes personal access tokens that haven't been used in 90 or more days.

controls.name: Token report and revoke (account console)
controls.what: Account admins list PATs across workspaces and revoke them.
controls.setting: Account console > Security > Token report; databricks token-management delete
controls.quote: select a token and click Revoke.

controls.name: IP access lists
controls.what: Restrict account console/account APIs and workspace/workspace APIs to approved IPs.
controls.setting: Account console IP access lists; workspace IP Access List API
controls.quote: The default allows connections from any IP address.

controls.name: Context-based ingress policies
controls.what: Account-level allow/deny rules combining identity, network source and request scope, e.g. pinning service principals to trusted networks.
controls.quote: allow and deny rules that combine who is calling, from where they are calling, and what they can reach

controls_unknown: No account-wide switch to disable PATs across all workspaces was found; the toggle is per workspace.
Whether IP access lists explicitly cover PAT/OAuth API calls is implied (workspace-level APIs) but not stated.
Whether context-based ingress rules can distinguish auth method (PAT vs OAuth) is not stated.
How to update or delete federation policies, and how to revoke an individual OAuth secret, were not covered on the fetched pages.
TTL min/max ranges, and whether built-in databricks-cli app follows app-connection TTL defaults, not confirmed.
Single-use refresh token details page returned 404; defaults per app not confirmed.
Azure/GCP capabilities and tiers not checked.

authentication.summary: OAuth user-to-machine and machine-to-machine, external token federation, and legacy personal access tokens.

federation.details: This path uses a local/static or platform-native credential. Evaluate a separate federation path where listed.

ip_restriction.boundary: Enterprise tier. Separate account/workspace IP lists protect public UI/API access; PrivateLink traffic is not filtered by them. Context-based ingress (Enterprise) can add rules combining identity (e.g. service principal), network source and access type.

lifetime.summary: Default maximum 730 days; admins can reduce it (new tokens only). Unused PATs are auto-revoked after 90 days.

renewal.summary: Admins can impose a shorter PAT maximum, control who can create/use PATs and revoke them. Setting custom max to 0 restores 730-day system default.

administration.summary: Service principals, entitlements/resource ACLs, federation policies, PAT controls and context-based ingress controls.
administration.conditions: AWS IP-access-list docs require Enterprise tier. Azure/GCP capabilities and licensing must be checked separately.

offboard.details: Tokens of a deactivated user stop working (they remain but cannot authenticate); SCIM removal deactivates the user.

inventory.details: Account console > Security > Token report; workspace Token Management API (databricks token-management list).

reads.api: SQL: SELECT * FROM system.access.audit WHERE service_name='workspace' AND action_name='workspaceExport' (filter user_identity.email)

offboard.ui: Remove the user from the IdP account-level SCIM connector (deactivates the user)

token_format.notes: Prefix from official legacy Tokens CLI example (dapi + 32 chars); regex inferred from example, not documented. GitHub type databricks_access_token, push protection and validity checks.

log_sources.name: Databricks audit logs (system.access.audit system table / audit log delivery)
log_sources.notes: Account- and workspace-level events; account-level rows have workspace_id 0. No general retention stated on the table page; events of a deleted workspace older than 14 days are removed.

log_sources.name: Account console token report / Token Management API
log_sources.notes: Lists token_id, owner_id, created_by_id, creation_time, expiry_time, last_used_day; filter by owner, workspace, last used.

credential_id_fields.notes: Hash of the token in lifecycle events

lifecycle_events.notes: Token dropped; also on user removal

anomaly_cues: tokenLogin for a tokenId from a new source_ip_address or user_agent
tokenLogin for a token owned by a deactivated or IdP-removed user
generateDbToken with long tokenExpirationTime created right after an interactive login from an unusual IP
burst of generateDbToken across workspaces by one user
GitHub secret scanning alert for databricks_access_token

containment.steps: Revoke: databricks token-management delete TOKEN_ID (DELETE /api/2.0/token-management/tokens/{token_id}) or account console token report > Revoke; owner can run databricks tokens revoke --token-id. Deactivate owner if compromised.
containment.notes: PAT is the bearer credential itself; docs do not state propagation delay. Tokens of deactivated users are not auto-revoked.

sample_query.query: SELECT request_params['tokenId'] AS token_id, user_identity.email, source_ip_address, user_agent, min(event_time) AS first_seen, count(*) AS uses FROM system.access.audit WHERE service_name = 'accounts' AND action_name = 'tokenLogin' AND event_date >= current_date() - INTERVAL 7 DAYS GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY first_seen DESC
sample_query.purpose: Find PATs used from new IPs or user agents

calls.reveals: Notebook or whole-directory contents (source code, sometimes embedded secrets/results)
calls.log_notes: Audit log / system.access.audit; user_identity shows the caller. Docs describe the event as a notebook export.

detections.title: Databricks TruffleHog Scan Detected
detections.detects: Any Databricks API request with a TruffleHog user agent, which indicates a leaked token being validated.

detections.title: Databricks Non-SSO Login Detected
detections.detects: Successful logins that did not use SAML SSO, including token logins with a PAT.
